top_story: A year into the Gaza truce, Israeli strikes that killed eight people on 1 October, including five in a civilian vehicle in Gaza City, underscored that the ceasefire has hardened into a condition of chronic insecurity in which civilians still see no safe refuge. Hours earlier, panic on a Dubai-to-Israel flight forced an emergency diversion to Saudi Arabia after an attacker entered the cockpit area and passengers subdued him, exposing how tension around Israel-linked travel is spilling into civilian transit routes beyond active war zones. The previous day’s reconstruction of the Minab school bombing in Iran, where 120 children were killed, revived one of the starkest symbols of U.S. wartime impunity and sharpened a regional climate in which older traumas and current violence reinforce public fear and anger. The wider picture is a region where civilian spaces—schools, roads, and aircraft cabins—are increasingly shaped by militarized politics, deepening social vulnerability far from any stable front line.
